newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police find 15th victim of serial killer.
newsitem.headline: S.African police find 15th victim of serial killer.

text.p: The corpse of a strangled woman, believed to be the 15th victim of the latest in South Africa's series of serial killers, was found on Wednesday.
"The woman had been strangled, possibly with her own clothing. Her panties were torn and marks around her private parts suggest she was also raped," a police statement said.
A spokesman said there was a strong possibility the case could be linked to a Johannesburg serial killer who police believe has also murdered 14 other women since May last year.

Dubbed the Nasrec murderer because many of the bodies were found near an exhibition centre with that name south of the city, the killer has been profiled as well dressed, suave and intelligent with a deep-seated hatred of women.
His victims are black females, mostly between the ages of 20 and 35, who are lured from minibus taxis.
The worst suspected murderer uncovered to date in South Africa, Moses Sithole, pleaded not guilty in court last month to 38 murders and 40 rapes.
Apart from Sithole, police have arrested six other alleged serial killers in the past two years -- three near Johannesburg, two in Cape Town and one in KwaZulu-Natal province.

The killings have terrified a nation, already popularly dubbed the world's most violent society outside of a war zone, particularly people in and around the industrial heartland of Johannesburg where 52 of an estimated 75 serial murders have been committed.
